description: Create a Zendesk ticket with a subject and initial comment, plus optional ticket properties such as priority, status, assignment, tags, collaborators, followers and custom fields. Returns the ticket ID, agent URL and selected ticket properties.

group_id.description: The ID of the group to assign the ticket to.
group_id.human_parameter_description: The Zendesk group ID the ticket should be assigned to. Groups are collections of agents.
group_id.title: Group Id

priority.description: Zendesk priority. Must be one of: 'urgent', 'high', 'normal', 'low'. Defaults to 'normal'.
priority.human_parameter_description: How urgent this request is and how quickly it needs attention. Choose urgent, high, normal, or low based on impact and time sensitivity. Defaults to 'normal'.
priority.title: Priority

requester_email.description: Email of the requester. Must accompany `requester_name`. Ignored if requester_id is provided.
requester_email.human_parameter_description: The requester's email address so they can receive ticket notifications. Include this only if you're also providing their name.
requester_email.title: Requester Email

requester_id.description: The ID of the user requesting support. If provided, requester_name and requester_email are ignored.
requester_id.human_parameter_description: The Zendesk user ID of the person reporting this issue. Use this if you know the user's ID, otherwise use requester_name/email.
requester_id.title: Requester Id

requester_name.description: Name of the requester. If you supply this, you MUST also supply `requester_email`. Leave both blank to default to the authenticated user. Ignored if requester_id is provided.
requester_name.human_parameter_description: Full name of the person reporting the issue or needing help. Provide this only if you're also adding their email so they receive updates.
requester_name.title: Requester Name

status.description: The state of the ticket. Allowed values: 'new', 'open', 'pending', 'hold', 'solved', 'closed'.
status.human_parameter_description: The current state of the ticket. Tickets typically start as 'new' and move through 'open', 'pending', 'hold', 'solved', and 'closed'.
status.title: Status

subject.description: Short summary of the issue. Keep it concise (e.g. 'Cannot log in').
subject.human_parameter_description: A short, clear title for the issue so support understands it at a glance. Keep it brief, like 'Can't log in' or 'Billing discrepancy'.
subject.title: Subject

tags.description: Array of tags to apply to the ticket.
tags.human_parameter_description: Labels to categorize or filter the ticket. Tags help with reporting and automation.
tags.title: Tags

ticket_form_id.description: The ID of the ticket form to render for the ticket. Enterprise only.
ticket_form_id.human_parameter_description: The ID of a custom ticket form to associate with this ticket. This feature requires an Enterprise plan.
ticket_form_id.title: Ticket Form Id

ticket_type.description: The type of this ticket. Allowed values: 'problem', 'incident', 'question', 'task'.
ticket_type.human_parameter_description: Categorize the ticket: 'problem' for root cause issues, 'incident' for occurrences of a problem, 'question' for inquiries, 'task' for work items.
ticket_type.title: Ticket Type

via_followup_source_id.description: The ID of a closed ticket to create a follow-up from. The new ticket will be linked to the source ticket.
via_followup_source_id.human_parameter_description: ID of a closed ticket this new ticket follows up on. Creates a link between tickets.
via_followup_source_id.title: Via Followup Source Id
